record.title: Sparse Autoencoder Hallucination-Subspace Identification and Causal Feature Suppression
record.statement: Large language models encode hallucination-prone generative states as a sparse, identifiable cluster of monosemantic SAE features in mid-to-late residual stream positions representing 'confident generation without factual grounding,' and causally suppressing this feature cluster via activation steering at inference time will measurably reduce hallucination rates on TruthfulQA, HaluEval, and FactScore.
record.mechanism:
The central mechanistic claim is that LLM hallucinations arise from a specific representational geometry that is invisible in raw neuron activations due to superposition, but becomes identifiable through SAE sparse decomposition.

Why superposition masks the hallucination signal: LLMs learn to represent 'genuine factual retrieval' and 'fluency-driven plausible completion' (the confabulation mode) using overlapping sets of neurons, because both modes produce syntactically coherent output and co-occur frequently during pretraining. Individual neurons therefore fire for both modes — they are polysemantic with respect to the factual/confabulation distinction. This is exactly the class of problem SAEs are designed to resolve.

Phase 1 — SAE training: A large overcomplete SAE (expansion factor ≥8x, e.g., d_model=4096 to d_SAE=32768 features) is trained with L1 sparsity regularization on residual stream activations drawn from layers 16-28 of a 7B+ parameter LLM (e.g., Llama-3-8B or Mistral-7B). These middle-to-late layers are targeted because mechanistic work on knowledge retrieval circuits shows that factual associations are resolved in this depth range. The SAE is trained unsupervised on general text; no hallucination labels are required at this stage.

Phase 2 — Contrastive feature identification: A contrastive dataset is constructed using TruthfulQA and HaluEval: for each prompt, model-generated continuations are partitioned into 'factual' and 'hallucinated' classes using ground-truth labels. SAE feature activation vectors are recorded at final entity-token or answer-onset positions. Sparse regression (LASSO) identifies features with significantly higher activation during hallucinated versus factual outputs. The hypothesis predicts a sparse differential profile concentrated in 50–500 features, whose human-audited semantics will relate to 'vague confident assertion,' 'approximate recall,' or 'plausible-but-unverified claim.' Conversely, features active during factual outputs will relate to specific entity grounding and high-confidence knowledge retrieval.

Mechanistic explanation: SAE decomposition reveals that the model has learned two distinct generative sub-programs occupying the same representational space via superposition: (A) a 'knowledge-anchored retrieval' sub-program activated when the model has strong associative evidence from training, and (B) a 'fluency-completion' sub-program activated when the model fills gaps using distributional plausibility heuristics. In raw activation space these are conflated. The SAE's overcomplete sparse decomposition resolves the superposition, yielding causally separable monosemantic features — a separation impossible with linear probes.

Phase 3 — Causal validation via activation steering: Two interventions validate causality: (a) Suppression: hallucination feature cluster directions are subtracted from the residual stream during inference (analogous to demonstrated concept-suppression in the Anthropic monosemanticity work). (b) Amplification: same features artificially amplified on correctly-grounded prompts should increase hallucination rates. Bidirectional causal control, plus specificity controls using random matched feature sets, establishes that these features are causally upstream rather than epiphenomenal correlates.

Phase 4 — Benchmark evaluation: Hallucination rates measured on TruthfulQA (truth rate), HaluEval (detection accuracy), and FactScore (factual precision) with/without suppression. Specificity control: perplexity on factual prompts must remain stable (<5% change), confirming the intervention targets only the confabulation subspace.

Scalability: Post-hoc SAE training on frozen LLM activations requires no base model fine-tuning. Inference-time intervention is an O(d_SAE) additive residual stream operation. Switch SAE architecture enables scaling to millions of features at frontier-model compute budgets.
record.anticipated_outcomes:
1. A sparse cluster of 50-500 SAE features will reliably activate during hallucinated outputs but not factual outputs across TruthfulQA and HaluEval.
2. Human annotators will rate hallucination-cluster features as interpretable and relating to 'vague/approximate confident assertion' or 'plausibility-driven completion without grounding,' confirming mechanistic interpretability rather than mere statistical correlation.
3. Suppressing the hallucination feature cluster at inference time will improve TruthfulQA truth rates by 10-25 percentage points and reduce HaluEval hallucination rates by 15-30%, with perplexity increase <5% on factual prompts.
4. Artificially amplifying the hallucination feature cluster on normally-factual prompts will increase hallucination rates by a comparable margin, establishing bidirectional causal control.
5. Suppressing a random matched-size set of non-hallucination SAE features will produce no significant hallucination reduction, confirming specificity of the identified subspace.
6. The hallucination subspace will exhibit cross-model conservation across Llama and Mistral families, suggesting a general transformer phenomenon rather than an idiosyncratic architectural artifact.
7. FactScore open-domain evaluation will show improved factual precision, confirming generalization beyond curated benchmark prompts.
record.novelty_argument:
1. Beyond linear probes: The survey (via AXBENCH benchmarking) notes SAEs can underperform linear probes on some tasks, but linear probes find a single direction in raw polysemantic space and cannot decompose the mechanism. This approach exploits SAE's unique ability to resolve superposition — isolating specific monosemantic features constituting the hallucination state, which is mechanistically richer than any linear direction in undecomposed space.

2. Mechanistic explanation vs. mere correlation: Representation engineering and probing classifiers identify correlates of hallucination but do not explain what those activations represent semantically. SAE decomposition produces human-auditable features that explain why the hallucination state exists — the model superimposes knowledge-retrieval and fluency-completion sub-programs, which only become separable after sparse decomposition.

3. Causal validation protocol: The bidirectional steering protocol (suppression reduces hallucination; amplification increases it) provides principled causal evidence beyond correlational methods. The survey identifies causal relevance as a key standard for mechanistic interpretability.

4. Intervention specificity via monosemanticity: Because SAE features are monosemantic, the intervention precisely targets the confabulation sub-program without collateral suppression of related features (e.g., general uncertainty expression or broader fluency generation). This precision is impossible with polysemantic probes.

5. Human-auditable hallucination mechanism: The approach produces a human-readable map of which specific features the model activates when hallucinating, enabling auditability of the mechanism — a capability unique to SAE decomposition.

6. Novel application domain for causal SAE intervention: While SAEs have demonstrated feature discovery and behavioral steering in general settings, their application to isolating and causally suppressing hallucination-specific representational states — validated with bidirectional causal probes and multi-benchmark quantitative evaluation — is not described in the surveyed literature.
